dripping of blood from his fingernails and toenails for the last year
occasional pus discharge
no history of preceding trauma or drug intake

violaceous discoloration of 7 fingernails and 3 toenails
longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation of the nail plate
partial to complete loss of nail plate with oozing of blood resulting in hemorrhagic crusting of the nail beds and folds
raised liver enzyme levels
positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status

concepts.why: The patient has a positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and histopathological findings consistent with lichen planus, including hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, and basal cell degeneration.
The patient presents with violaceous discoloration, longitudinal ridging, and partial to complete loss of the nail plate, which are characteristic features of nail lichen planus.

aliases: lichen planus of the oral mucosa
concepts.why: The patient has lichenoid plaques on the oral mucosa, which is a common manifestation of oral lichen planus.
The patient has a positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and raised liver enzyme levels, which are indicative of hepatitis C virus infection.

rationales.F01: Painful swelling of the proximal nail folds is a characteristic feature of nail lichen planus and can be associated with hepatitis C-associated lichen planus.
rationales.F02: Dripping of blood from fingernails and toenails is a distinctive feature of nail lichen planus.
rationales.F05: Lichenoid plaques on the oral mucosa are a hallmark of oral lichen planus and can be associated with hepatitis C-associated lichen planus.
rationales.F10: Positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status is a strong indicator of hepatitis C virus infection and can be associated with hepatitis C-associated lichen planus.
rationales.F11: Histopathological features such as hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, basal cell degeneration, and dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate are characteristic of lichen planus.

frontier_selector.rationale: The combination of positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status, lichenoid plaques in the oral mucosa, and characteristic nail changes supports Hepatitis C-associated lichen planus as the most comprehensive diagnosis.
